stories.headline: Magyar visits Brussels before inauguration, reports 'successful' talks on unlocking €17 billion in frozen EU funds
stories.summary: Incoming Prime Minister Péter Magyar made a pre-inauguration trip to Brussels on 29 April, meeting European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President António Costa. Magyar described the talks as 'extremely constructive and successful,' saying the frozen funds — including €10.4bn in Covid recovery money that must be unlocked before an August deadline — would 'soon arrive' in Hungary. Von der Leyen pledged Commission support for reform alignment. Magyar confirmed he will return to Brussels the week of 25 May as PM to finalise a formal political agreement.

stories.headline: Tisza cabinet finalized but nepotism accusations fly over Magyar's brother-in-law as justice minister
stories.summary: Magyar completed his 16-member Tisza government lineup, with the most controversial appointment being his brother-in-law Márton Melléthei-Barna as justice minister — a role central to rule-of-law reform. Magyar defended the choice on merit, but faced criticism from Fidesz, Mi Hazánk's Toroczkai, and even some Tisza supporters. The cabinet also includes Anita Orbán (foreign minister), Gábor Pósfai (interior), and government commissioners Radnai Márk and Rost Andrea.

stories.headline: Orbán offers to resign as Fidesz leader but party defers decision to June congress
stories.summary: Viktor Orbán offered his resignation as president of Fidesz on 28 April, but the party's national board reportedly declined to vote on it, deferring the matter to a party congress scheduled for 13 June. Orbán also announced he would not sit in parliament as an opposition MP, saying he is needed in rebuilding the 'patriotic movement.' Media and analysts have been closely tracking every signal about Orbán's political future, including speculation about an MEP seat for immunity.

Orbán argued the ruling represents political overreach and a violation of Hungarian sovereignty and constitutional identity.

stories.headline: MNB holds interest rate at 6.25%, Varga Mihály pledges cooperation with Tisza but warns on inflation and credit ratings
stories.summary: The Hungarian National Bank's Monetary Council unanimously held the base rate at 6.25% at its first post-election meeting on 28 April. Governor Varga Mihály pledged to support the incoming Tisza government's economic policy 'if we know what it means and if it doesn't fuel inflation,' and said the MNB would assist law enforcement investigating the Matolcsy-era foundation scandal. He also cautioned that credit rating agencies will expect a credible medium-term fiscal path by autumn, and expressed reservations about the speed of euro adoption.

stories.headline: Magyar proposes meeting with Zelenskyy over Ukrainian-Hungarian minority rights, conditions EU accession support
stories.summary: Incoming PM Magyar proposed a meeting with Ukrainian President Zelenskyy in western Ukraine to discuss the rights of the ethnic Hungarian minority in Transcarpathia, stating Hungary will not support Ukraine's EU accession unless Kyiv restores cultural, linguistic, and education rights. Zelenskyy indicated he would meet Magyar in some form and said 'there will be no problem' on the minority issue. Bloomberg reported Magyar raised the same conditions with European Council President Costa in Brussels.

stories.headline: May 9 inauguration celebrations planned at Kossuth Square; Magyar clashes with Budapest Mayor Karácsony over competing events
stories.summary: Magyar detailed a full-day 'system-change' public celebration for 9 May — the date the new parliament convenes, Magyar is elected PM, and takes the oath of office — at Kossuth Square and along the Danube embankment. Controversy erupted when Budapest Mayor Gergely Karácsony announced a 'system farewell' concert for the preceding evening (May 8) at a nearby location; Magyar publicly criticized the move as 'harmful and rude,' questioning whether the bankrupt capital would foot the bill. The Hungarian Defence Forces were also confirmed to participate in the inauguration ceremonies.

stories.headline: Sulyok loses Holy Crown vote, presidency future uncertain as Tisza holds removal power
stories.summary: President Tamás Sulyok's proposal to move the Holy Crown of Hungary to the parliament's plenary chamber for the incoming MPs' oath was blocked by the Holy Crown Council, in a symbolic defeat ahead of the transfer of power. Separately, media and legal commentators debated whether Magyar would seek Sulyok's removal given the Tisza supermajority, while a pro-Sulyok petition attracted fewer than 100,000 signatures despite Orbán amplifying it. Sulyok also pre-emptively signed off several decisions before the government handover, including awarding a state decoration to Trócsányi László.

stories.headline: NKA cultural fund scandal: Fidesz distributed 17+ billion HUF to loyalist performers before election
stories.summary: Investigation and media coverage revealed that the outgoing Fidesz government distributed more than 17 billion HUF through a special National Cultural Fund (NKA) committee to artists, musicians, and organisations linked to Fidesz in the run-up to the election. Outgoing Culture Minister Hankó Balázs defended the grants as merit-based but faces calls to resign from the incoming health minister. Several prominent performers linked to the grants drew further scrutiny, including violinist Mága Zoltán whose associate's company received 500 million HUF.

stories.headline: Index newspaper forced to publish court-ordered correction admitting its Fidesz-era 'Tisza tax plan' articles were false
stories.summary: Index.hu, regarded as a government-aligned outlet, published a court-ordered correction admitting that documents it had promoted during the election campaign as the Tisza Party's tax plan were not, in fact, Tisza's documents and that no valid conclusions could be drawn from them. Magyar publicly demanded a front-page correction displayed for days, describing the original articles as the 'biggest lies' of the campaign. The court had previously ordered the correction and Index also owed HUF 500,000 in legal costs.
